description: Actual-source review of the evidence relevant to Brali's WOOP / mental contrasting with implementation intentions protocol. The reviewed evidence supports MCII as a bounded self-regulation strategy for goal pursuit, but not a guarantee of goal achievement, not one universal effect size for every person or goal, and not a substitute for addressing external constraints. A 2026 academic-procrastination RCT already present in Brali's research queue is reviewed here as narrow corroborating evidence rather than duplicated or generalized beyond its undergraduate setting.

crossref:10.1016/j.actpsy.2025.106168.review_notes: Source review completed for the WOOP/MCII Gold boundary. The randomized study involved 81 undergraduates at one private Chinese university, compared MCII with a positive-thinking control, and followed outcomes for one week. Retain as narrow support for obstacle-plus-plan task initiation in this context only; do not generalize to universal anti-procrastination, long-term goal achievement, workplaces, clinical populations, or treatment.

research_candidates.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Mental Contrasting With Implementation Intentions on Goal Attainment
research_candidates.review_notes: The full open-access meta-analysis was reviewed. It included 21 empirical articles contributing 24 independent effect sizes and 15,907 participants. The random-effects pooled effect was small-to-medium (Hedges' g=0.336, 95% CI 0.229 to 0.443) with medium heterogeneity (I2=59.321%). Publication-bias analyses were mixed; trim-and-fill produced a smaller adjusted estimate (0.242, 95% CI 0.143 to 0.342). The authors explicitly called for more studies on moderators.

evidence_decisions.source_title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Mental Contrasting With Implementation Intentions on Goal Attainment
evidence_decisions.citation_text: Wang G, Wang Y, Gai X. Frontiers in Psychology. 2021;12:565202.
evidence_decisions.study_design: Random-effects meta-analysis of 21 empirical articles contributing 24 independent MCII effect sizes across field interventions and goal domains, with 15,907 participants in total.
evidence_decisions.population: Children, college students and adults across academic, health, relationship and personal goal contexts represented in the included intervention studies. The corpus was heterogeneous and was dominated numerically by two very large MOOC samples.
evidence_decisions.intervention_or_exposure: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions: identify a desired future and an obstacle in reality, then form an if-obstacle-then-behavior plan. Delivery varied between experimenter-led and document-based interventions.
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: Across the included field-intervention studies, mental contrasting with implementation intentions was associated with a small-to-medium average improvement in goal attainment. The pooled random-effects estimate was Hedges' g=0.336, while publication-bias adjustment produced a smaller estimate. This supports WOOP/MCII as a bounded self-regulation option for feasible goals, not as a guarantee of individual goal success.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: WOOP guarantees that a person will achieve a goal.
The pooled effect size applies to every person, goal domain or delivery format.
WOOP is always better than mental contrasting or implementation intentions used separately.
A document or self-guided WOOP exercise is as effective as an experimenter-led intervention.
The meta-analysis establishes a clinically meaningful treatment effect.
The study proves that one fixed WOOP script is optimal.
limitations: The included studies were heterogeneous in population, goal domain, intervention delivery and outcome measurement.
The meta-analysis reported medium heterogeneity and mixed publication-bias diagnostics; trim-and-fill yielded a smaller adjusted estimate.
Two very large MOOC studies accounted for most participants and were excluded from moderator analyses because of their numerical dominance.
The number of studies was limited for moderator inference, and the authors explicitly called for additional studies.
An average standardized effect cannot predict whether the protocol will help one individual with one goal.
evidence_decisions.notes: Editorial outcome: retain WOOP as reviewed practical self-regulation guidance for meaningful, reasonably feasible goals. Keep the user-visible wording focused on the obstacle-to-if-then planning process and an observable attempt, not a promise of goal attainment or an advertised effect size.

evidence_decisions.source_title: Beyond positive thinking: A randomized trial of mental contrasting with implementation intentions to curb academic procrastination
evidence_decisions.citation_text: Zhou X, Wider W, Wu H, Xu Y, Qin M, Borromeo AS. Acta Psychologica. 2026;262:106168.
evidence_decisions.study_design: Randomized controlled comparison of MCII with a positive-thinking strategy control, with pre-test, post-test and one-week follow-up outcomes.
evidence_decisions.population: 81 undergraduate students at a private Chinese university in an academic-procrastination context.
evidence_decisions.intervention_or_exposure: MCII applied to academic procrastination compared with a positive-thinking strategy control.
evidence_decisions.supported_claim: In this specific undergraduate academic-procrastination study, MCII reduced task aversiveness and improved willingness to initiate academic tasks relative to a positive-thinking control, with effects reported through one-week follow-up. It provides narrow corroborating evidence for the obstacle-plus-plan mechanism in an academic setting.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: This trial proves WOOP works for all goals or populations.
The trial establishes long-term goal achievement effects.
The results generalize to workplaces, clinical populations or high-stakes decisions.
A one-week follow-up establishes durable behavior change.
limitations: The sample was small and restricted to undergraduates at one private Chinese university.
The context was academic procrastination rather than general goal pursuit.
The follow-up was one week, so long-term persistence is unknown.
The outcomes reported in the abstract do not justify generalizing to broad life outcomes or clinical treatment.
evidence_decisions.notes: Use as corroborating boundary evidence only. Reuse the existing research-candidate identity; do not turn this narrow RCT into the primary public claim or imply cross-domain efficacy.
